binding.note: the on-disk builder has since gained its R-309 self-stamp, so its current hash NO LONGER equals the build-time hash. The binding was verified AT THE TIME, before that edit: builder-at-commit was byte-identical to builder-on-disk, content sha 028bc06928f3b9a8. Recording the drift rather than hiding it -- a proof that silently re-derives itself later is not a proof.

status: EVIDENCE ARTIFACT — records a binding, asserts no result
supersedes_need_for_this_check: from the next build onward the tape carries builder_sha256 in its own header and this class of sidecar is unnecessary
tree_state_at_build: git status EMPTY on all five producing files
why_this_exists: R-309 accepted, for THIS DIAGNOSTIC_NEVER_EVIDENCE artifact only, that the tape records builder_REF without a builder CONTENT hash. A ref is a pointer: it names a commit to go look at, it does not establish that the file which ran matches it. This artifact supplies that proof EXTERNALLY so a reader who was not present can check it. It is strictly weaker than an in-band stamp, which is why the builder now self-stamps (same commit) and why in-band is mandatory for anything result-bearing.
